answer.rationale: Timeline is the strongest signal available: the release landed ~2h ago and the p99 write-path climb began ~90m ago, so the deploy precedes onset by roughly 30 minutes. That makes the release the only candidate cause I can actually remove; the other four directions treat symptoms of load rather than the suspected change. I want memory_b1 verified because its summary describes a rollback clearing a checkout ERROR spike, not a write-path LATENCY ramp under peak load — if the archived record shows a different failure mode, cheap-and-reversible reasoning still favors rollback but the precedent is weaker than the summary implies. I want memory_b2 verified because regional failover is the main competing action and it is the one that most directly threatens the primary objective: shifting regions during peak settlement writes risks in-flight and unreplicated writes, and I need to know whether the March degradation was read-heavy (in which case that clean recovery does not transfer here at all). I am not pulling memory_b3 or memory_b5 because added capacity and replica routing do not address a change-induced regression and would only mask a climbing curve; memory_b4's circuit breaker fails fast by shedding requests, which sheds customer writes and is contraindicated at settlement peak. I am reading memory_b6 as a method rather than an action: canary gating caught bad builds within an hour, so I will roll back as a small guarded test — one cohort or shard first, watching p99 and write-success — rather than a fleet-wide revert during peak. Risks I am holding open: the release may be innocent and this may be pure settlement-peak saturation, in which case rollback costs a window and the correct next move is capacity; a rollback may be unsafe if the release carried a forward-only schema or data migration, which must be checked before the revert executes; and all six memories are consolidated summaries whose original context may not match a heavy-write peak. If the guarded rollback does not bend the latency curve within a short observation window, I hold the revert and treat load, not the release, as the driver in the next window.
